name: Adriano Santos
action: Adriano sets down the lug wrench, straightens up from the snare, and answers the phone. He speaks in his usual loud, flat tone: "Marina. Alright, I'll come. But I'm not staying the whole afternoon—the wrap is giving me trouble and my ears are ringing. I'll be there for lunch, sit near you, and if the noise gets to me I'll step out to the garage for a while. Don't save me any dessert."
reason: Adriano's initial impulse was to stall—to give an excuse about the drum and his ear—but he also felt a pull to say yes to spare Marina's worry. In reflection, he recognized the call as a test of whether he would keep disappearing, and he remembered the family table and his father's pattern of stepping out rather than staying away entirely. This strengthened his inclination to go, but he kept a boundary rooted in his legitimate physical discomfort and unfinished work. The revised tendency—committing to attend but clearly limiting his stay—shows in his spoken answer: he says he will come, acknowledges the wrap and his ears, and signals that he may slip out to the garage if overwhelmed. He does not make another excuse, but he does not promise full participation, preserving the conflict between protecting his peace and honoring family connection.
